outcome: No unconditional answer has appeared since 26 January 2024. The one new substantive preprint in the window, Berarducci and Gallinaro (arXiv:2603.08365, March 2026, revised June and September 2026), axiomatizes the complete theory of the real exponential field under Schanuel's conjecture and so recovers the 1996 Macintyre–Wilkie decidability under that hypothesis; it adds an unconditional model-completeness result for exp restricted to (-1,1) but no unconditional decision procedure. Other in-window work is partial: a 2025 Pisa master's thesis (not publicly consultable) claims an arithmetical bound Δ⁰₂ on the existential fragment, which is not a decision procedure; a 2025 paper decides a restricted exponential on a different question; and Schanuel-conjecture neighbours bear only on the hypothesis. No AI system is credited with any part of this.
problem_asks: Single question: is the first-order theory of the real numbers with the exponential function decidable? Parts: (1) the structure, the real field with addition, multiplication, order and a unary exponential function exp (standard reading: Rₑₓₚ, with the first-order language of ordered rings plus exp); (2) the property asked, that the set of first-order sentences true in that structure is decidable, i.e. there is an algorithm that decides truth for every sentence. The statement names no sub-cases and no weaker form. It asks for an unconditional yes-or-no answer. Nothing in the statement fixes an answer; both 'decidable' and 'undecidable' would resolve it.

events.what_happened: van den Dries, 'The field of reals with a predicate for the powers of two', Manuscripta Mathematica 54 (1985) 187–195. Shows the reals with a predicate for the integer powers of 2 admit quantifier elimination in an expanded language, hence are decidable. Neighbour result on a different structure (predicate for 2^n, not exp). Date and content taken from the Avigad–Yin arXiv abstract (opened); the 1985 paper itself was not opened.
events.delivers: Decidability of the reals with a predicate for 2^n (integer powers of two). This is a different structure: it adds a predicate for a discrete set of powers, not the exponential function on all reals. It does not decide Rₑₓₚ.
events.remains: Everything in the problem as stated: the full exp function on all reals, and its first-order theory.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published in Manuscripta Mathematica 54 (1985); the referee process was not examined
checked_by.where: Citation via arXiv:cs/0610117 (opened); the 1985 paper not opened

events.direction: Positive for a different (discrete-power) structure. Cuts neither way on Rₑₓₚ.

events.what_happened: Macintyre and Wilkie, 'On the decidability of the real exponential field', in Kreiseliana: About and Around Georg Kreisel (ed. P. Odifreddi, A K Peters, Wellesley, 1996, pp. 441–467). Under the real form of Schanuel's conjecture, shows that Th(Rₑₓₚ) is decidable: they give an algorithm that tests whether an exponential polynomial over Q has a real zero, and isolate a 'weak Schanuel' condition equivalent to decidability of the theory. Content as described by the 2026 Berarducci–Gallinaro introduction (opened) and search snippets; the 1996 chapter itself was not opened.
events.delivers: Conditional decidability of the full first-order theory of Rₑₓₚ, on the hypothesis that the real Schanuel conjecture holds (a restricted form of Schanuel's conjecture for real numbers). It also reduces decidability to an effective procedure for exponential polynomials with integer coefficients. Unconditional decidability is not established.
events.remains: Unconditional decidability of Th(Rₑₓₚ): the hypothesis is open. Nothing unconditional on the question as stated.

checked_by.what_they_did: Wrote a zbMATH review of the volume (Zbl 0896.03012, 1998), per a search snippet

events.time_since_posted: about 30 years; re-derived by Berarducci–Gallinaro in 2026
events.doubts: No active reason to doubt is recorded. The sources do not say whether the 1996 chapter's argument is the one Berarducci–Gallinaro re-derive; that is inferred from their statement that their result implies the Macintyre–Wilkie theorem.
events.direction: Conditional positive: the theory is decidable if the real Schanuel conjecture holds. Does not settle the unconditional question either way.

events.what_happened: A. J. Wilkie, 'Model completeness results for expansions of the ordered field of real numbers by restricted Pfaffian functions and the exponential function', Journal of the American Mathematical Society 9 (1996) 1051–1094. Proves that Rₑₓₚ is model complete (every formula is equivalent to an existential one) and, with Khovanskii's finiteness theorem, o-minimal. Opened only through the Berarducci–Gallinaro introduction; the 1996 paper itself was not opened.
events.delivers: Model completeness and o-minimality of Rₑₓₚ. This reduces the decidability question to existential sentences but decides nothing on its own.
events.remains: The whole decidability question: the problem asks for decidability, and model completeness is a tool, not an answer.

checked_by.where: JAMS 9 (1996) 1051–1094, per the Berarducci–Gallinaro introduction (opened); the journal page not opened

events.direction: Neither way. A structural result that is the starting point for the reduction to existential formulas.

events.what_happened: Achatz, McCallum and Weispfenning, 'Deciding polynomial-exponential problems', ISSAC 2008 (Linz/Hagenberg, 20–23 July 2008), pp. 215–222, ACM. Gives an unconditional decision procedure for a restricted class of prenex first-order sentences over the reals built from integer-coefficient polynomials and exp, where only the outermost quantified variable occurs inside exp. Implemented in REDLOG. Opened only through the repository summary (snippet); the paper was not opened. A 2006 Macquarie technical report with a similar scope ('cylindrical analytic decomposition') is also reported in a repository summary and was not opened; if it covers exp, the first public written argument would be 2006.
events.revisions: A 2006 Macquarie technical report with similar scope is reported (repository summary, not opened); not dated against this event.
events.delivers: Unconditional decidability of one restricted class: prenex sentences with integer-coefficient polynomials and exp in which only the outermost quantified variable appears inside exp. This is a restricted case of the problem's full theory, not the theory itself.
events.remains: Sentences with exp applied to several or inner quantified variables; the full first-order theory of Rₑₓₚ.

checked_by.qualification: Refereed conference in symbolic and algebraic computation
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted into ISSAC 2008 proceedings (per repository record)
checked_by.where: Macquarie University research repository record (snippet only; not opened)

machine_checked.system: REDLOG (implementation of the procedure, not a proof check)

events.doubts: The procedure's correctness and scope rest on the ISSAC paper, which was not opened. The restriction (only the outermost quantified variable inside exp) is the reason the result is partial.
events.direction: Positive decidability for a fragment: a restricted class of sentences, not the full theory. Cuts toward decidability only in part.

events.what_happened: Gareth Jones and Tamara Servi, 'On the decidability of the real field with a generic power function', Journal of Symbolic Logic 76(4) (2011) 1418–1428. Shows the theory of the real field expanded by a generic real power function x^α (α not 0-definable in Rₑₓₚ) is decidable relative to an oracle for the cut of α in Q. Also gives generic computable reals and a decidable o-minimal expansion by an analytic function. The authors frame it as a step toward Tarski's question. Manchester eprint deposited 4 July 2011 (opened); JSL publication from snippet.
events.revisions: Manchester eprint deposited 4 Jul 2011, marked as differing slightly from the version to be published in JSL; JSL 76(4) 2011 per listing.
events.delivers: Decidability of the real field with a generic power function, relative to an oracle for the cut of the exponent. This is a different structure from Rₑₓₚ: it adds x^α, not exp. It is decidable only relative to an oracle.
events.remains: Rₑₓₚ itself, with the full exponential function; the unrelativised decidability question.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published in JSL 76(4) 2011 (per the eprint page's journal note and search listing)

events.direction: Positive for a different structure (generic power function, relative to an oracle). Cuts neither way on Rₑₓₚ.

events.what_happened: McCallum and Weispfenning, 'Deciding polynomial-transcendental problems', Journal of Symbolic Computation 47(1) (January 2012) 16–31. Generalises the 2008 fragment procedure to a class of transcendental functions, listed as including exp(x), ln(x) and arctan(x), for prenex sentences with the same restriction (only the outermost quantified variable inside the transcendental function). Abstract seen via the Macquarie repository summary; not opened.
events.delivers: Unconditional decidability of the same restricted class of prenex sentences, extended to several transcendental functions including exp. Still restricted to sentences with the outermost-variable restriction; it does not give the full first-order theory of Rₑₓₚ.
events.remains: Sentences in which exp is applied to inner or several variables; the full first-order theory of Rₑₓₚ.

checked_by.where: Macquarie University research repository (snippet only; not opened)

events.doubts: Scope read from a repository summary only; the full abstract and proofs were not read.
events.direction: Positive for a restricted class of sentences. Cuts toward decidability only in part.

events.what_happened: Alessandro Berarducci (with Marcello Mamino), talk 'o-minimal EXP-fields and Schanuel's conjecture', Fields Institute Workshop on Tame Geometry, online, 6 June 2022, presented as work in progress. Assuming Schanuel's conjecture and using ideas of Wilkie, the residue structure of an o-minimal EXP-field (which carries an induced exponential making it a model of Tₑₓₚ, per Krapp) embeds into the field, so Schanuel's conjecture implies every o-minimal EXP-field has an archimedean substructure. The open question raised is whether that substructure is elementary. No written version was found, so the talk date stands in for the first public argument; the 2022 date is before the window whichever date applies.
events.delivers: Conditional on Schanuel's conjecture: an archimedean substructure in every o-minimal EXP-field. Whether this substructure is elementary is left open. Concerns the Transfer Conjecture route, not directly decidability.
events.remains: Elementarity of the archimedean substructure; the Transfer Conjecture; decidability.
events.time_since_posted: about 4 years; no written version found
events.direction: Conditional partial. Neither way on decidability.

events.what_happened: Lothar Sebastian Krapp, 'Embedding the prime model of real exponentiation into o-minimal exponential fields', arXiv:2302.01609 (v1 3 Feb 2023; v2 31 Jul 2023), Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society 56 (2024) 907–913. Assuming Schanuel's conjecture, the prime model of real exponentiation embeds into every o-minimal exponential field, but not necessarily elementarily. The unconditional part is an embeddability result via König's Lemma. Motivated by decidability and the Transfer Conjecture; it claims neither.
events.revisions: v1 3 Feb 2023; v2 31 Jul 2023; BLMS 56 (2024) 907–913 (year only in journal reference).
events.delivers: Conditional on Schanuel's conjecture: a non-elementary embedding of the prime model of real exponentiation into any o-minimal exponential field. Non-elementarity means it does not give the Transfer Conjecture, so it does not yield decidability.
events.remains: Decidability of Rₑₓₚ; the Transfer Conjecture (an elementary version of the embedding).

checked_by.who: Referees of the Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society

events.direction: Conditional partial. Neither confirms nor refutes the Transfer Conjecture, and does not settle decidability.

events.what_happened: Omri Isac, Yoni Zohar, Clark Barrett and Guy Katz, 'DNN Verification, Reachability, and the Exponential Function Problem', arXiv:2305.06064 (submitted 10 May 2023; v2 10 Jul 2023), CONCUR 2023 (LIPIcs vol. 279, pp. 26:1–26:18 per search listing). Theorem 1: the decidability of verifying DNNs with a particular set of piecewise-smooth activations (including sigmoid and tanh) is equivalent to Tarski's open problem. Theorem 2: verification against quantifier-free linear arithmetic specifications reduces to DNN reachability, whose approximation is NP-complete.
events.revisions: v1 10 May 2023; v2 10 Jul 2023 (current on arXiv page as fetched); CONCUR 2023 version per search listing.
events.delivers: Equivalence (reduction) between a neural-network verification question and the open problem. Establishes no decision procedure and no undecidability result for the exponential theory.
events.remains: Everything in the problem as stated.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted to CONCUR 2023 (LIPIcs vol. 279) per search listing

events.direction: Reduction only: links a verification question to the problem. Cuts neither way on the problem itself.

events.what_happened: Teemu Hankala, Miika Hannula, Juha Kontinen and Jonni Virtema, 'Complexity of Neural Network Training and ETR: Extensions with Effectively Continuous Functions', arXiv:2305.11833 (19 May 2023), published AAAI 2024 (per search listing; not opened). Shows that training networks with sigmoid activation is polynomial-time bireducible with the existential theory of the reals with exp (ETRₑₓₚ); thus sigmoid training is solvable exactly when ETRₑₓₚ is decidable. Gives upper bounds in low arithmetical levels for the general training problem and shows sinusoidal activations make training undecidable.
events.revisions: Single arXiv version (19 May 2023); AAAI 2024 publication per search listing.
events.delivers: Reduction: the sigmoid training problem is equivalent to the existential theory ETRₑₓₚ. Upper bounds for the training problem are in low arithmetical levels (not given specifically for ETRₑₓₚ in the abstract read). No decision procedure.
events.remains: Decidability of ETRₑₓₚ and of the full theory of Rₑₓₚ.
events.direction: Reduction only. Cuts neither way on the problem itself.

events.what_happened: Jorge Gallego-Hernández and Alessio Mansutti, 'On the Existential Theory of the Reals Enriched with Integer Powers of a Computable Number', arXiv:2502.02220 (v1 4 Feb 2025; v2 6 Feb 2025; v3 14 Oct 2025; v4 31 Aug 2026, current). Extended version of a STACS 2025 paper, submitted to LMCS. Treats the existential theory of the reals with a predicate for the integer powers of a fixed computable real r > 0. Undecidable if r is given only by a machine; decidable if r is transcendental (known) or algebraic; under a polynomial-root-barrier assumption, complexity bounds apply (NEXPTIME, EXPSPACE, 3EXP for a family including π and e). Also: the entropic-risk threshold problem for stochastic games (base e, algebraic aversion factor) is in EXP without Schanuel's conjecture.
events.revisions: v1 4 Feb 2025; v2 6 Feb 2025; v3 14 Oct 2025; v4 31 Aug 2026 (current).
events.delivers: Decidability results for a different theory: the existential theory with a predicate for integer powers of one fixed r (e being an example of r), not the exponential function on all reals. Also an unconditional EXP bound for one stochastic-games problem.
events.remains: The full exponential function x ↦ eˣ on all reals; the full first-order theory of Rₑₓₚ.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted to STACS 2025 (per the arXiv comment field); PDF fetch of the STACS paper did not decode

events.doubts: Scope is a different question (predicate for powers of r, not exp). Not a doubt about correctness.
events.direction: Different question: decidability and complexity for a restricted exponential. Cuts neither way on the full theory of Rₑₓₚ.

events.what_happened: Michel Waldschmidt, 'Schanuel Property for Elliptic and Quasi-Elliptic Functions', arXiv:2504.14041 (submitted 18 Apr 2025), Hardy–Ramanujan Journal (vol. 48, 2025; publication date reported on the journal listing as 27 Apr 2026, search snippet). For almost all complex n-tuples, a strong form of Schanuel's conjecture holds (the 2n numbers x_i and exp(x_i) are algebraically independent); similar statements for elliptic and quasi-elliptic functions. A neighbour result about the hypothesis that Macintyre–Wilkie use, not about the problem.
events.revisions: v1 18 Apr 2025 (only version on arXiv page as fetched); journal version per listing.
events.delivers: A measure-theoretic statement: strong Schanuel for almost all complex tuples, plus algebraic-independence examples for elliptic functions. It does not give the full Schanuel conjecture for all tuples, and it is for complex tuples, not the real form used by Macintyre–Wilkie.
events.remains: Full Schanuel conjecture for every tuple; the real form; and so decidability of Rₑₓₚ.
events.doubts: Read from the abstract only, which says almost all tuples and does not mention the real form. Inference that it does not help the real hypothesis is the reader's, not the paper's.
events.direction: Neither way on the problem. Partial progress on a hypothesis (complex, almost all), not on decidability.

events.what_happened: Master's thesis 'On the Real Exponential Field', Università di Pisa, Dipartimento di Matematica, examination session starting 9 May 2025 (per the ETD record). Supervisors Marcello Mamino and Francesco Paolo Gallinaro. Fully consultable PDF. Per the ETD abstract summary: two parts: model completeness results for the reals with restricted Pfaffian chains and for Tₑₓₚ (Wilkie); decidability results that follow from Schanuel's conjecture (Wilkie and Macintyre), and a bound due to Kirby on the size of the essential counterexample set to Schanuel's conjecture. Expository and conditional; no unconditional result is claimed.
events.delivers: Expository. Restates the conditional Macintyre–Wilkie decidability under the real Schanuel hypothesis and the model completeness results. No new unconditional result is claimed in the abstract.

checked_by.what_they_did: Examined the thesis in the May 2025 session (session date only, per ETD record)

events.direction: Conditional expository. Neither way on the unconditional question.

events.what_happened: Master's thesis 'Existential Theory of the Reals, Neural Networks, and Tarski's Exponential Function Problem', Università di Pisa, examination session starting 9 May 2025 (ETD record), supervisors Tamara Servi and Arnaud Durand. Author named as Lucio Tanzini in the IMJ-PRG seminar listing and search snippets; the ETD page does not show the name. Not publicly consultable (restricted). Per the ETD abstract summary: Chapter 3 shows that the existential theory of the reals with exp (ETRₑₓₚ) is Δ⁰₂ in the arithmetical hierarchy (computable from the halting problem); improving to Σ⁰₁ or Π⁰₁ would be equivalent to solving the problem, per Macintyre–Wilkie. Also: an approximate-training problem for neural networks is poly-time bireducible with ETR; ETR with a finite set of effectively continuous functions is Σ⁰₂ and the bound is sharp. Under the assumption that Rₑₓₚ is effectively exponentially bounded, ETRₑₓₚ is ω-r.e. The same content was given in a seminar at IMJ-PRG on 3 Nov 2025 (opened).
events.revisions: Seminar 'O-minimality meets computability, with applications to neural networks', IMJ-PRG, 3 Nov 2025, same content per listing.
events.delivers: An arithmetical-hierarchy upper bound, Δ⁰₂, for the existential fragment ETRₑₓₚ. It is a bound on complexity, not a decision procedure, and it is not decidability: the thesis says a Σ⁰₁ or Π⁰₁ bound would be equivalent to solving the problem. Restricted to existential sentences; by model completeness of Rₑₓₚ, existential decidability is equivalent to full decidability.
events.remains: A computable decision procedure for ETRₑₓₚ and for the full theory of Rₑₓₚ; the gap between Δ⁰₂ and Δ⁰₁.

events.what_happened: Jonathan Pila, 'Combining the conjectures of Schanuel and Zilber–Pink', Rendiconti Lincei: Matematica e Applicazioni 36(3) (2025), pp. 653–670, DOI 10.4171/RLM/1086, published online 4 March 2026 (per EMS page). Formulates a single conjecture strictly equivalent to the conjunction of Schanuel's conjecture and the multiplicative Zilber–Pink conjecture. Neighbour result about the hypotheses, not about the problem. The EMS page gives submission 27 Apr 2025, acceptance 1 Jul 2025 and publication 4 Mar 2026; the first public version was not checked.
events.revisions: Earlier public version (if any) not checked.
events.delivers: A reformulation: one conjecture equivalent to the conjunction of Schanuel's conjecture and multiplicative Zilber–Pink. It proves neither conjecture.
events.remains: Both conjectures, and so the real Schanuel hypothesis that the decidability argument needs.

events.what_happened: Alessandro Berarducci and Francesco Gallinaro, 'On the elementary theory of the real exponential field', arXiv:2603.08365 (math.LO; 34 pages; posted 9 March 2026; preprint, no journal reference). Assuming the real Schanuel conjecture (SCᵣ), the complete theory Tₑₓₚ of Rₑₓₚ is axiomatized by the axioms of definably complete exponential fields satisfying exp′ = exp (main theorem: under SCᵣ, the definably complete theory T^dc_exp is complete, Theorem 14.3 in the HTML excerpt read). This implies the Macintyre–Wilkie decidability theorem under the same hypothesis. The unconditional ingredient is model completeness of the definably complete theory of exp restricted to (-1,1) (Theorem 12.4). The paper calls an unconditional polynomial-boundedness of the restricted theory an open problem. Acknowledgements thank Marcello Mamino (unpublished joint result) and Antongiulio Fornasiero; funding PRIN 2022. No AI or computer assistance is mentioned in what was read. Gallinaro gave the talk 'On the elementary theory of the real exponential field' at the Séminaire Général de Logique, IMJ-PRG, 16 Feb 2026 (opened), before the arXiv posting; the posting date is taken as the first written argument.
events.revisions: v1 9 Mar 2026 (38 KB); v2 23 Jun 2026 (40 KB); v3 25 Sep 2026 (41 KB, current). The content of the v2 and v3 changes was not identified.
events.delivers: Conditional on the real Schanuel conjecture: a complete axiomatization of Tₑₓₚ and therefore decidability of Th(Rₑₓₚ), recovering Macintyre–Wilkie under the same hypothesis. Unconditionally: model completeness of the definably complete theory for exp restricted to (-1,1), a restricted exponential, not the full Rₑₓₚ. So no unconditional decision procedure for the full theory is delivered.
events.remains: Unconditional decidability of Th(Rₑₓₚ); the real Schanuel hypothesis itself; the polynomial-boundedness of the restricted theory (the paper calls it open).
events.time_since_posted: about 7 months (posted 9 Mar 2026; latest version 25 Sep 2026)
events.direction: Conditional positive: under SCᵣ the theory is decidable, via a new axiomatization that recovers Macintyre–Wilkie. Unconditionally it is silent on the question as stated.

summary: Found and read: one substantive in-window preprint (Berarducci–Gallinaro, arXiv:2603.08365, 9 Mar 2026; v2 23 Jun 2026; v3 25 Sep 2026). From the arXiv abstract page, its HTML (first ~100k of 154k characters, plus a targeted second chunk for theorem statements), and the Pisa seminar listing (16 Feb 2026), the theorem is conditional on the real Schanuel conjecture: under it, Tₑₓₚ is axiomatized by definably complete exponential fields with exp′ = exp, which recovers Macintyre–Wilkie decidability (1996). The unconditional piece is model completeness for exp restricted to (-1,1). No independent written engagement with it was found, and no citing paper was found; so far the only qualified readers of the result are its two authors. The problem as stated (unconditional decidability of Rₑₓₚ) is still open on every source read. The in-window neighbours are partial: a Pisa master's thesis (Tanzini, May 2025, not publicly consultable) claims an arithmetical bound Δ⁰₂ on the existential fragment ETRₑₓₚ, which the thesis itself says is not a decision procedure; Gallego-Hernández and Mansutti (Feb 2025) decide the existential theory of reals with a predicate for integer powers of a fixed computable r, a different question; Waldschmidt (Apr 2025) and Pila (Mar 2026) bear on the Schanuel hypothesis only. Pre-window events are also recorded: Macintyre–Wilkie 1996 (the conditional decision result), Wilkie 1996 (model completeness), the 2008 and 2012 Achatz–McCallum–Weispfenning and McCallum–Weispfenning procedures (an unconditional decision procedure for a restricted class of prenex sentences with exp, implemented in REDLOG; the ISSAC 2008 paper itself was not opened), Jones–Servi 2011 (a generic power function, relative decidability), Krapp 2023 and the 2022 Berarducci–Mamino talk (conditional embeddings), and Isac et al. and Hankala et al. 2023 (reductions of neural-network verification and training to the exponential problem). Close calls: (1) whether a conditional decidability theorem resolves the problem; the record has the conditional result dated to 2026 and the unconditional status unchanged; (2) whether a Δ⁰₂ bound counts as moving the problem, since it is a complexity bound on the existential fragment and not decidability; (3) whether the 2008 and 2012 restricted-class decision procedures count as a case of the problem, since they cover only prenex sentences with exp applied to the outermost variable. For AI: the only AI-lab announcement reviewed was OpenAI's Astra list of ten problems (1 Aug 2026, via a DataCamp summary, not OpenAI's post), which does not include this problem. No event credits an AI system. Source notes: Ressayre's alternative proof of model completeness is dated 1991 in the Encyclopedia of Mathematics (snippet, not opened) and cited as [Res93] in the Berarducci–Gallinaro bibliography (per a search summary); not resolved. The Berarducci–Gallinaro introduction (HTML, opened) states that the real form of Schanuel's conjecture is not necessary, with weak Schanuel equivalent to decidability; a search summary says the same, and the Macintyre–Wilkie paper itself was not read. The Tarski high-school-algebra SAT paper (arXiv:2608.08421) is a different problem, and a 2026 lecture-notes chapter (arXiv:2604.25733) that calls this problem open appeared in snippets only; neither is counted as an event.
competing_reading: Read the 2026 Berarducci–Gallinaro axiomatization as real progress on the problem: it characterizes the complete theory of Rₑₓₚ, which the 1996 Macintyre–Wilkie argument did not, and a counter in the judging pass could treat a conditional theorem as a settled case, making the problem 'conditionally resolved' since 1996 with a new route in 2026. The opposite reading, which this record follows, is that every unconditional quantity is unchanged: the decision question still lacks an unconditional answer, the 2026 result restates a known decidability under the same hypothesis, and the in-window bounds (Δ⁰₂) are complexity statements on a fragment, not decidability.
what_would_settle_it: An unconditional decision procedure for Th(Rₑₓₚ), or a proof of undecidability, would settle the problem. Short of that, the status of Berarducci–Gallinaro depends on referee or journal treatment and on whether a later paper removes the real Schanuel hypothesis from their theorem (the published version or a later version of arXiv:2603.08365 would show this). The Δ⁰₂ claim needs the Tanzini thesis text, which is not publicly consultable. The ISSAC 2008 and JSC 2012 procedures need their full texts to confirm the restriction stated in the repository summaries.

judgement.why: The statement asks for an unconditional yes/no on decidability of Th(R_exp). Results conditional on (real) Schanuel's conjecture — Macintyre–Wilkie 1996, Berarducci–Gallinaro 2026, Krapp, the 2022 talk — answer a changed question with an extra hypothesis, so are variant; results on other structures (powers of 2, powers of r, generic power function) and on the Schanuel hypothesis itself (Waldschmidt, Pila) are variant too. Reductions (Isac et al., Hankala et al.), model completeness and the expository Pisa thesis settle nothing: none. The close call is Tanzini's Δ⁰₂ bound on ETR_exp: the statement names no quantity, only decidability, and an arithmetical-hierarchy placement that the thesis itself says falls short of the question does not move anything the statement asks, so none rather than bound (it is also unconsultable). The 2008/2012 restricted-fragment procedures decide a class of sentences of the theory itself, so case, but they are pre-snapshot and only partial. No AI involvement in any event.
judgement.doubts: Tanzini thesis scored none rather than bound; if arithmetical-complexity placement counted as a bound, it would be an unreviewed-content bound from a non-public thesis (examination committee treated as digestion). Scope of the 2008/2012 fragment results rests on repository summaries only.
